subject.title: fix(memory): use FTS-only when optional embeddings are unavailable

question: Should an existing semantic memory index whose optional embedding provider becomes unavailable remain searchable through its current FTS rows in read-only mode, rather than reporting memory unavailable until credentials return?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and session-state policy change: it improves recall availability while intentionally serving an index that cannot sync during the provider outage.

options.title: Accept read-only FTS recovery
options.body: Approve the proposed optional-provider behavior: preserve vector rows, allow keyword recall from existing FTS rows, and defer all index updates until embeddings are available again.

options.title: Keep the unavailable behavior
options.body: Require optional-provider failures on an existing semantic index to remain unavailable until credentials return, avoiding stale recall at the cost of losing keyword access.

recommendation.title: Accept read-only FTS recovery
recommendation.body: Approve the proposed optional-provider behavior: preserve vector rows, allow keyword recall from existing FTS rows, and defer all index updates until embeddings are available again.

likelyOwner.reason: The related current-main review documented the optional-provider versus explicit-provider contract and is the strongest available owner signal for this policy choice.
